statement: In the repository, recorded test fixtures must live under resources/fixtures/recorded and scope test fixtures under resources/fixtures/scopes.

quote: Language-specific parsing is defined in the `resources/queries/*.scm` files
statement: In the repository, language-specific tree-sitter parse patterns must be defined in resources/queries/*.scm files, not in TypeScript code.

quote: Packages starting `lib-` are only used internally in this monorepo and are not published to npm. Changing the api surface is fine as long as every place that consumes the api within this repository is updated.
statement: In packages/lib-*, a change to an exported API must update every consumer of that API within the repository.

quote: When writing or updating `.scope` files please follow the guidelines in [scope-test-format.md](./packages/app-web-docs/src/docs/contributing/scope-test-format.md)
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, scope test files should follow the style guidelines in packages/app-web-docs/src/docs/contributing/scope-test-format.md.

quote: Tests should be included for new functionality
statement: In the repository, new functionality should be accompanied by tests.

quote: Make sure changes are consistent with the project architecture
statement: In the repository, code changes should be consistent with the project architecture.

quote: we have a convention that any test that must be run within a VS Code context (eg because it imports `"vscode"`), should be placed in a file with the suffix `.vscode.test.ts`.
statement: In the repository, a test file that must run in a VS Code context (e.g. imports "vscode") must be named *.vscode.test.ts.

quote: All other tests should end with just `.test.ts`. This allows us to run non-VS Code tests locally outside of VS Code using `pnpm test`.
statement: In the repository, test files that do not need VS Code must be named *.test.ts (not *.vscode.test.ts) and must not import "vscode".

quote: We do not consider a bug fixed or feature added until there is a test (with an exception if writing the test is unreasonably difficult, in which case we'll usually file an issue to track adding a test).
statement: In the repository, every bug fix or feature must include a test unless writing one is unreasonably difficult.

quote: Note that it does not actually contain any tests itself; those are either embedded in `.test.ts` files either next to the code they're testing or in standalone `*-e2e` packages.
statement: In the repository, tests must be in .test.ts files next to the code they test or in standalone packages/*-e2e packages, not in packages/test-runner.

quote: These packages should expose `typecheck`, but they should not expose public `build`, `compile`, or `clean` scripts.
statement: In source-only shared code packages (e.g. packages/lib-common, packages/lib-engine), package.json should expose a typecheck script and must not expose build or compile scripts.

quote: These packages export source directly from `src`, and they should not rely on an `out` directory as part of their package contract.
statement: In source-only shared code packages, package.json exports should point to source under src (./src/index.ts), not to an out directory.

quote: These packages expose `bundle` scripts instead of `build` scripts. For example: - `bundle` - `bundle:dev` - `bundle:watch`
statement: In internal asset packages (e.g. packages/lib-cheatsheet-local, packages/lib-vscode-tutorial-webview), package.json should expose bundle / bundle:* scripts instead of build scripts.
In top-level application packages (packages/app-*), package.json should expose typecheck, dev and build scripts.

quote: `build` scripts should be self-contained. If a top-level package depends on internal bundle-producing packages, its `build` script should invoke their `bundle` scripts itself.
statement: In top-level application packages, the build script should be self-contained and invoke the bundle scripts of the internal packages it depends on.

quote: If more advanced hot-deploy behavior is needed, it should still hang off the top-level `dev` entrypoint rather than reintroducing older script names like `build:dev`.
statement: In top-level application packages, package.json must not define a build:dev script; development workflows should hang off the dev script.

quote: do not use root-level `compile` or generic `watch:*` scripts
statement: In the root package.json, scripts must not include compile or generic watch:* scripts.

quote: For internal source-only packages, `typecheck` should not create an `out` directory.
statement: In internal source-only packages, the typecheck script/tsconfig should not emit an out directory (noEmit).

quote: If your package is not a top-level application package, add a `"private": true,` line to your `package.json`.
statement: In packages/*/package.json, a package that is not a top-level application package must set "private": true.

quote: Internal source-only packages should generally just expose `typecheck`, and if needed `test`.
statement: In internal source-only packages, package.json scripts should be limited to typecheck and, if needed, test.

quote: If your package is a top-level application package, you will usually also want `dev` and `build`, and possibly helper `bundle:*` scripts if it produces internal artifacts for another package.
statement: In top-level application packages, package.json should define dev and build scripts, using bundle:* names for helper scripts producing internal artifacts.

quote: Mark each applicable `textFragment.xxx` facet as `supported` in the language's scope support table.
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/scopeSupportFacets/<language>.ts, each applicable textFragment.* facet must be marked supported.

quote: Add an `@textFragment` capture for each applicable text region in the language's query file. Capture the text content without its syntactic delimiters when the parse tree permits it.
statement: In resources/queries/<language>.scm, each applicable text region (strings, comments) must have an @textFragment capture, which should exclude the syntactic delimiters (e.g. via #child-range!) when the parse tree permits.

quote: Add fixtures for each supported text-fragment facet using the scope test recorder described below.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes, each textFragment facet marked supported for a language must have a scope test fixture.

quote: If one of the above facets doesn't apply to your language, you can mark it as `notApplicable` instead of `supported`. If the facet _**does**_ apply to your language, but you'd prefer to add support for it in a follow-up PR, you can mark it as `unsupported`.
statement: In language scope support tables, facets that do not apply to the language should be marked notApplicable, and applicable but not yet implemented facets marked unsupported.

quote: Note that you use the scope identifier (`@namedFunction`), _**not**_ the facet identifier (`@namedFunction.class`).
statement: In resources/queries/*.scm, captures must use the scope type identifier (e.g. @namedFunction), not the facet identifier (e.g. @namedFunction.class).

quote: If your language is not in that list, you need to find a VS Code extension that adds support for your language, and add the id of the given extension to [`packages/lib-common/src/extensionDependencies.ts`]
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/extensionDependencies.ts, the VS Code extension id must be listed for every supported language not natively detected by VS Code.

quote: Create a file with your scope support map to indicate which scopes you support. See eg [`markdown.ts`]
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/scopeSupportFacets/, each supported language must have its own <language>.ts file exporting a <language>ScopeSupport constant typed LanguageScopeSupportFacetMap.

quote: Add an entry pointing to your support table to [the global scope support table](../../../../../packages/lib-common/src/scopeSupportFacets/languageScopeSupport.ts)
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/scopeSupportFacets/languageScopeSupport.ts, every language scope support table must be registered.

quote: Create an empty `.scm` file in [`resources/queries/`](../../../../../resources/queries) to hold your parse tree patterns. It should be named after your language, eg `java.scm`.
statement: In resources/queries/, each language's parse tree patterns must be in a .scm file named after the language id (e.g. java.scm).

quote: The generated file is named after the language ID, for example `java.mdx`, and should not be edited manually.
statement: In packages/app-web-docs/src/docs/user/languages/*.mdx, generated language pages must not be edited manually; they are produced by meta-updater.

quote: Note that it is preferred to use `@foo.leading` or `@foo.trailing` instead of `@foo.removal` in situations where you just need to include a leading or trailing delimiter in the removal range.
statement: In resources/queries/*.scm, @<scope>.leading / @<scope>.trailing captures should be used instead of @<scope>.removal when only a leading or trailing delimiter needs to be included in the removal range.

quote: Thus, it should nearly always appear in a separate pattern from the scope itself
statement: In resources/queries/*.scm, @<scope>.iteration captures should appear in a separate pattern from the scope's own capture.

quote: unlike the other aspects, which must appear in the same pattern as the scope itself.
statement: In resources/queries/*.scm, relationship captures (@<scope>.domain, .leading, .trailing, .removal, .interior) must appear in the same pattern as the scope's own capture.

quote: Use `@G_` followed by at least two underscore-separated scope names to give the same capture to multiple scopes. ... Every scope name in the group must be valid.
statement: In resources/queries/*.scm, @G_ group captures must list at least two underscore-separated scope names, each a valid scope type.

quote: The format is automatically generated, so you shouldn't need to edit it yourself.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, the scope snapshot sections should be generated by the test updater rather than edited by hand.

quote: We try to keep this as short and simple as possible while still containing the syntax you want to test.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, the source code section should be as short and simple as possible while containing the syntax under test.

quote: For classes, functions and variables we use the classic: `foo`, `bar`, `baz`, `bongo`. Language specific formatting still applies. eg `Foo` for a class in Java, `IFoo` for an interface in C# etc.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, class, function and variable names must be foo, bar, baz, bongo (with language-specific casing such as Foo or IFoo).

quote: For arguments and parameters we use: `aaa`, `bbb`, `ccc` and so on.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, argument and parameter names must be aaa, bbb, ccc and so on.

quote: For data type we use `int` or `number`.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, data types in examples must be int or number.

quote: For value we use `0`, `1`, `2` and so on.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, literal values in examples must be 0, 1, 2 and so on.

quote: Don't add more lines than the example actually needs. ... Keep the code single line and with an empty body if possible.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, examples must not have more lines than needed and should be single-line with an empty body where possible.

quote: When testing a facet inside a code block. eg a method in a class or a field in a interface multiple lines are prefered.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.scope, facets tested inside a code block (e.g. a method in a class) should use a multi-line example.

quote: If you're doing a `*.iteration.document` test we want to include a leading and trailing new line.
statement: In resources/fixtures/scopes/**/*.iteration.document*.scope tests, the source code must begin and end with an empty line.

quote: Please try to keep the file as small as possible, though.
statement: In resources/fixtures/recorded/**/*.yml, the initial document of a recorded test should be as small as possible.

quote: If a kind of spoken form is missing, add its raw Talon list to `state.json` rather than adding cheatsheet-specific assembly to Talon.
statement: In cursorless-talon, missing spoken-form kinds should be exposed as raw Talon lists in state.json rather than by adding cheatsheet-specific assembly code on the Talon side.
In the committed Algolia crawler-settings.js config, the apiKey field must be "<REDACTED>" and never a real key.
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint correctness-category rules are enabled at warn (lint:ts runs with --deny-warnings).
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint suspicious-category rules are enabled at warn.
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint pedantic-category rules are enabled at warn.
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint perf-category rules are enabled at warn.
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint style-category rules are enabled at warn (except those listed in disabledRules).
In all oxlint-linted JS/TS files, all oxlint restriction-category rules are enabled at warn (except those listed in disabledRules).

quote:
// Disabled since nursery contains rules under development that may change
// nursery: "warn",
statement: In all oxlint-linted files, the oxlint nursery category is deliberately not enabled.
In all linted files, arrow function body style (braces vs expression body) is not enforced.
In all linted files, comments are not required to start with a capital letter.
In all linted files, class methods are not required to use this.
In all linted files, cyclomatic complexity is not limited.
In all linted files, identifier length is not restricted (short names like i, x are allowed).
In all linted files, variables are not required to be initialized at declaration.
In all linted files, multiple classes per file are allowed.
In all linted files, function length in lines is not limited.
In all linted files, file length in lines is not limited.
In all linted files, the number of function parameters is not limited.
In all linted files, the number of statements per function is not limited.
In all linted files, await inside loops is allowed.
In all linted files, console.* calls are allowed.
In all linted files, continue statements are allowed.
In all linted files, comparing with == null / != null is allowed.
In all linted files, an if statement as the only statement in an else block is allowed.
In all linted files, functions created inside loops are allowed.
In all linted files, numeric literals (magic numbers) are allowed inline.
In all linted files, negated conditions in if/else and ternaries are allowed.
In all linted files, ++ and -- operators are allowed.
In all linted files, variable shadowing is allowed.
In all linted files, ternary expressions are allowed.
In all linted files, using undefined as an identifier/value is allowed.
In all linted files, leading/trailing underscores in identifiers are allowed.
In all linted files, using functions/variables before their definition is allowed.
In all linted files, the void operator (e.g. void promise) is allowed.
In all linted files, there is no requirement on combining or splitting variable declarations.
In all linted files, destructuring is not required for property/array access.
In all linted files, regex capture groups are not required to be named.
In all linted files, import sorting is not enforced by the linter.
In all linted files, object keys are not required to be sorted.
In all linted files, variables within a declaration are not required to be sorted.
In all linted files, both function declarations and function expressions/arrow functions are allowed.
In all linted files, exports are not required to come after other statements.
In all linted files, exports are not required to be grouped into a single export statement.
In all linted files, the number of imported modules per file is not limited.
In all linted files, named exports are allowed.
In all linted files, namespace imports (import * as x) are allowed.
In linted files generally (outside the lib-common/lib-engine override), importing Node.js built-in modules is allowed.
In all linted files, relative imports from parent directories (../) are allowed.
In all linted files, a single-export module is not required to use a default export.
In all linted files, returning after invoking a callback is not enforced.
In all linted files, synchronous Node APIs (e.g. fs.readFileSync) are allowed.
In all linted files, top-level await is allowed.
In all linted files, async/await is allowed.
In all linted files, barrel files (index.ts re-exporting modules) are allowed.
In all linted files, spreading objects inside map callbacks is allowed.
In all linted files, optional chaining (?.) is allowed.
In all linted files, object rest/spread properties are allowed.
In all linted files, .then() callbacks are not required to return a value.
In all linted files, new Promise(...) construction is allowed.
In all linted files, callback-style APIs are allowed instead of await.
In React components, passing newly created (inline) functions as JSX props is allowed.
In React components, className/style props on components are allowed.
In React components, JSX nesting depth is not limited.
In React components, string literals directly in JSX are allowed.
In React components, using array indexes as key props is allowed.
In React files, multiple components per file are allowed.
In React files, exporting non-component values alongside components is allowed.
In React files, React is not required to be imported in scope for JSX.
In TypeScript files, explicit function return type annotations are not required.
In TypeScript files, constructor parameter properties (e.g. constructor(private foo: Foo)) are allowed.
In TypeScript files, function parameters are not required to have readonly types.
In TypeScript files, functions returning promises are not required to be marked async.
In TypeScript files, returning values from void-typed callbacks is not flagged.
In all linted files, file name casing is not enforced (camelCase and PascalCase file names are both allowed).
In all linted files, the depth of nested function calls is not limited.
In all linted files, passing function references directly to array methods (e.g. arr.map(fn)) is allowed.
In all linted files, an if statement as the sole statement inside another if block is allowed.
In all linted files, negated conditions are allowed (unicorn variant).
In all linted files, the null literal is allowed.
In all linted files, object literals as default parameter values are allowed.
In all linted files, explicitly passing or returning undefined is allowed.
In all linted files, index access like arr[arr.length - 1] is allowed instead of .at().
In all linted files, EventEmitter is allowed instead of EventTarget.
In all linted files, CommonJS constructs (require, module.exports, __dirname) are not flagged.
In all linted files, alternatives to Number() coercion are not flagged.
In all linted files, getElementById/getElementsBy* are allowed instead of querySelector.
In all linted files, consecutive calls (e.g. multiple push calls) are not required to be merged into one.
In all linted files, Array.from/concat/slice are allowed instead of spread syntax.
In all linted files, simple if/else statements are not required to be rewritten as ternaries.
In all linted files, postMessage calls are not required to pass a targetOrigin.
In all linted files, switch case clauses are not required to be wrapped in braces.
In all linted files, comparisons must use === / !== except comparisons with null, which must use == null / != null.
In all linted files, a module must not be imported in more than one import statement, except that a separate `import type` from the same module is allowed.
In all linted files, code must not import node:assert; it must import node:assert/strict instead.

quote: patterns: [{ group: ["../*/src", "../*/src/*", "../../*/src", "../../*/src/*"], message: "Relative package imports are not allowed" }]
statement: In all linted files, code must not import another package's src via relative paths (../*/src, ../../*/src/*); it must import the package by name (e.g. @cursorless/lib-common).
In all linted files, unused variables and arguments are not allowed unless their name starts with _ (rest siblings are ignored).
In all linted files, side-effect-only imports (import "x") must not be used, except for .css files.
In all linted files, comments must not contain TODO.
In the repository, JSX must only appear in files with the .tsx extension.
In TypeScript files, the oxlint typescript plugin rules (type-aware) are enabled across all warn-level categories.
In .js files, files are not required to be unambiguous ES modules (import/unambiguous off).
In .ts (non-tsx) files, React rules-of-hooks is not enforced.
In *.test.ts files, function expressions are not required to be named.

quote: files: ["packages/app-vscode/src/scripts/**/*.ts"], "no-restricted-imports": ["warn", { paths: [{ name: "vscode", message: "Scripts shouldn't depend on vscode" }] }]
statement: In packages/app-vscode/src/scripts/**/*.ts, code must not import "vscode".
In packages/lib-common/**/*.ts and packages/lib-engine/**/*.ts, code must not import Node.js built-in modules (node:fs, node:path, etc.).
In lib-common/lib-engine test files, packages/lib-engine/src/scripts/** and packages/lib-engine/src/testUtil/**, importing Node.js built-in modules is allowed.

quote: files: ["packages/lib-common/src/types/command/**/*.ts"], patterns: [{ group: ["@cursorless/*", "../*"], message: "API types shouldn't have any dependencies" }]
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/types/command/**/*.ts, code must not import @cursorless/* packages or anything from a parent directory (../*).

quote: paths: [{ name: "@*", message: "API types shouldn't have any dependencies" }]
statement: In packages/lib-common/src/types/command/**/*.ts, code must not import any scoped (@*) package.
In Python files (cursorless-talon, cursorless-talon-dev, etc.), ruff pycodestyle (E) rules must pass.
In Python files, ruff Pyflakes (F) rules must pass (no unused imports/variables, undefined names).
In Python files, ruff pyupgrade (UP) rules must pass (modern Python 3.11 syntax), except the ignored UP007/UP045/UP035.
In Python files, ruff flake8-bugbear (B) rules must pass.
In Python files, ruff flake8-simplify (SIM) rules must pass, except SIM105.
In Python files, imports must be sorted per ruff isort (I) rules.

quote: "C4", # Catch incorrect use of comprehensions, dict, list, etc
statement: In Python files, ruff flake8-comprehensions (C4) rules must pass.
In Python files, modules must be imported with conventional aliases per ruff flake8-import-conventions (ICN).
In Python files, ruff flake8-return (RET) rules must pass.
In Python files, ruff refurb (FURB) rules must pass.

quote: "FLY", # Checks for str.join calls that can be replaced with f-strings.
statement: In Python files, static str.join calls must be replaced with f-strings per ruff flynt (FLY).
In Python files, line length is not enforced by ruff (E501 off).
In Python files, try/except/pass is allowed instead of contextlib.suppress (SIM105 off).

quote: "UP007", # Union[X, Y] -> X | Y not supported in Talon 0.4 actions
statement: In Python files, Union[X, Y] annotations are allowed (UP007 off) because X | Y is not supported in Talon 0.4 actions.

quote: "UP045", # Optional[X] -> X | None not supported in Talon 0.4 actions
statement: In Python files, Optional[X] annotations are allowed (UP045 off) because X | None is not supported in Talon 0.4 actions.
In Python files, deprecated imports (e.g. typing.List, typing.Callable) are not flagged (UP035 off).
In Python files, code must target Python 3.11 (the Python version of public Talon 0.4).
In Python files, pyright does not require the first method parameter to be named self/cls (Talon action classes).
In Python files, pyright does not report imports whose module source is missing.
In Python files, pyright does not report unresolved imports (e.g. the talon module).
In Lua files, luacheck warning 432 (shadowing an upvalue argument) is not enforced.
In Lua files, vim is the only declared extra global; other undeclared globals are flagged by luacheck.
In Lua files, code must only use the LuaJIT standard library globals.
In Lua files, lua-language-server treats vim, talon, it and describe as known globals and targets Lua 5.1.
In CSS/SCSS files, an empty line before at-rules is not required (stylelint at-rule-empty-line-before disabled).

quote: - id: forbid-symlinks name: Forbid symlinks entry: Forbid symlinks language: fail types: [symlink]
statement: In the repository, committed files must not be symlinks.

quote: - id: check-recorded-test-marks files: ^resources/fixtures/recorded/.*/[^/]*\.yml$ entry: pnpm transform-recorded-tests --check-marks
statement: In resources/fixtures/recorded/**/*.yml, initialState.marks must contain exactly the marks targeted by the command plus any listed in marksToCheck (compared after grapheme normalization), as checked by packages/lib-engine/src/scripts/transformRecordedTests/checkMarks.ts.
